peerMapping.justification: Three-run Kimi K3 consensus selected only the displayed peers: NVDA 35.6% with 3/3 replicate support; MSFT 25.4% with 3/3 replicate support; AMD 11.9% with 3/3 replicate support; XYZ100 10.2% with 2/3 replicate support; AMZN 8.5% with 2/3 replicate support; GOOGL 8.5% with 2/3 replicate support. Individual rationales state each economic relationship.

peers.name: NVIDIA
peers.reason: NVIDIA is the closest economic comparator because Nebius sells AI cloud capacity built largely on NVIDIA GPUs and related data-center systems. NVDA captures the same AI accelerator demand, supply availability, pricing cycle, and capex sensitivity that drive Nebius revenue and valuation, and it is a directly traded underlying rather than a leveraged wrapper.

peers.name: Microsoft
peers.reason: Microsoft is Nebius's anchor customer through a multi-year AI infrastructure agreement worth roughly 17 to 19 billion dollars, making it the largest direct driver of Nebius's contracted revenue visibility and a first-order return comparator. It also proxies hyperscale AI compute demand. This major-customer relationship earns the second-largest weight.

peers.name: Advanced Micro Devices
peers.reason: AMD is the second major GPU/accelerator supplier into AI data centers and a potential diversification source for Nebius's compute hardware, so it shares the same AI accelerator demand cycle and data center capex exposure as Nebius's core input cost.

peers.name: Nasdaq-100
peers.reason: The primary hedge is also a peer because Nasdaq-100 captures a large share of Nebius return exposure through the dominant systematic and sector index for AI-heavy growth equities. The weight is large for index co-movement, not because the index is an economic substitute; its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 196.139 USD millions and is only an execution tie-breaker.

peers.name: Amazon
peers.reason: Amazon, through AWS, is one of the largest AI cloud infrastructure providers and competes for the same enterprise AI workloads that underpin Nebius's neocloud model; its capex-driven AI buildout cycle is a close demand analogy for Nebius's revenue exposure.

peers.name: Alphabet
peers.reason: Alphabet operates Google Cloud and its own AI compute infrastructure, competing directly in the market for GPU-accelerated cloud capacity; its returns embed the same hyperscaler AI capex and cloud demand factors that move Nebius.

primary_index_hedge.name: Nasdaq-100
primary_index_hedge.reason: Nasdaq-100 is the best eligible primary hedge because Nebius is a Nasdaq-listed AI infrastructure equity whose dominant generic risk is mega-cap technology and AI growth beta. It is classified as equity_index, and its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 196.139 USD millions; that liquidity helps execution, but the hedge is chosen for systematic and sector exposure rather than as a business substitute.

peerMapping.historyMethod: daily-rebalanced peer spot total returns using the fixed Kimi weights; the basket begins with the first available selected peer, unavailable pre-listing peers are omitted, and remaining weights are renormalized; the browser rebases the basket to the target spot level at the first shared date of each selected chart range

liveSplice.method: current Hyperliquid native or TradeXYZ perp mid divided by that peer's matching-venue perp close on its latest spot date; available Kimi weights are renormalized and applied as a one-period return from the published peer spot endpoint; USD cash close is retained for disclosure but never mixed with a differently scaled perp contract

earningsOptions.source: Schwab listed-options chain, FMP earnings calendars, and Sharadar adjusted prices

liquidityFilter.sides: OTM puts below spot and OTM calls above spot

model.name: liquid vertical-spread risk-neutral CDF
model.description: Liquid vertical spreads are used when the chain supplies at least four valid probability points; otherwise the nearest liquid ATM straddle supplies the expiration distribution. Earnings-date log distances are time-scaled from the first post-event expiration.
model.measure: risk-neutral, not a historical or physical forecast

historicalAnalysis.eventSource: SEC earnings release history with FMP historical calendar fallback
historicalAnalysis.method: Each current two-leg structure is translated into percentage-of-spot strikes and debit. Those same normalized strikes and today's debit percentage are replayed across prior earnings using the same calendar-day entry lead and post-event exit horizon. A profitable event requires expiration payoff greater than the original debit.
historicalAnalysis.limitation: Stock-path proxy using today's premium; historical option quotes, bid-ask execution, volatility repricing, early exercise, dividends, and transaction costs are not reconstructed.
